record.paper_title: Free Boundary Minimal Surfaces in the Unit Ball: Recent Advances and Open Questions
record.original_question: For sufficiently large genus g, there are two families of embedded free boundary minimal surfaces in B^3 described in the survey: the desingularization examples Σ_g^{KL} and the equivariant min-max examples Σ_g^K, each having genus g, three boundary components, and the same dihedral symmetry. For all sufficiently large g, are these two surfaces actually congruent to one another, meaning the same surface up to rigid motions of B^3?

evidence.quote: Open Question 4. For all g sufficiently large, are the surfaces Σ_g^{KL} and Σ_g^K congruent to each other?
Given that the topology and the symmetry group are the same as those constructed in Theorem 3.9, it is reasonable to ask the following:

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $B^3 \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ denote the closed Euclidean unit ball. A properly embedded surface $\Sigma \subset B^3$ with $\partial\Sigma \subset \partial B^3 = S^2$ is called a free boundary minimal surface if it has zero mean curvature in $B^3$ and meets $S^2$ orthogonally along $\partial\Sigma$.

Two known constructions produce, for every sufficiently large integer $g$, an embedded free boundary minimal surface in $B^3$ of genus $g$ with exactly three boundary components and invariant under the dihedral group $D_{g+1}$ (acting by rotations about a fixed axis through angles that are multiples of $2\pi/(g+1)$ together with a reflection):

(a) A desingularization construction $\Sigma_g^{\mathrm{KL}}$, obtained by desingularizing the union of the critical catenoid and the equatorial disk (which intersect orthogonally inside $B^3$) along their circle of intersection by gluing in scaled Scherk-type singly periodic minimal surfaces, producing for all sufficiently large $g$ an embedded free boundary minimal surface of genus $g$ with three boundary components and the above dihedral symmetry.

(b) An equivariant min-max construction $\Sigma_g^{K}$, obtained as a min-max critical point of the area functional in the class of $D_{g+1}$-equivariant sweepouts of $B^3$, yielding for each sufficiently large $g$ an embedded free boundary minimal surface of genus $g$ with three boundary components and the same dihedral symmetry.

Question: Is it true that for all sufficiently large $g$, the surfaces $\Sigma_g^{\mathrm{KL}}$ and $\Sigma_g^K$ are congruent, i.e., they coincide up to a rigid motion of $B^3$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether the Kapouleas–Li desingularization family and Ketover's equivariant min-max family of free boundary minimal surfaces in $B^3$ coincide is described in the literature as a plausible but unresolved conjecture; no proof of congruence (or of non-congruence) appears to have been published. Recent works on equivariant min-max and free boundary minimal surfaces (through 2023–2025) continue to refer to this identification as open.

status_evidence.title: Free boundary minimal surfaces in the unit three-ball via desingularization of the critical catenoid and the equatorial disc (Kapouleas–Li)
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of high-genus free boundary minimal surfaces by desingularizing the critical catenoid and equatorial disk; notes that it is plausible these surfaces coincide with Ketover's min-max examples.
status_evidence.claim: The relationship between the two families is suggested but not proved.

status_evidence.title: Equivariant index bound for min–max free boundary minimal surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Ketover's equivariant min-max free boundary minimal surfaces with dihedral symmetry and three boundary components, comparing with desingularization constructions.
status_evidence.claim: The identification of the two families remains an open question in subsequent literature.
